explanations: The defect is docs.forEach(async (doc) => ...) in indexPage. forEach ignores the promises the async callback returns, so indexPage resolves immediately, before any upsert finishes. runOnce then saves the cursor and calls refresh() while upserts are still running, and any upsert rejection becomes an unhandled rejection instead of failing the run. If the process dies or an upsert fails, the cursor has already moved past documents that were never indexed, so they are silently skipped. Use await Promise.all(docs.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await.

Inside the loop, cursors.save runs after await this.indexPage(...) and after the `if (!page.nextCursor) break` check, so it saves only when a next cursor exists. It is not saved before listing, not once at the end, and refresh() runs after the loop.

Both analyze calls are started inside Promise.all and the result is awaited, so they run concurrently and both finish before the fields object is built. They are not sequential, the await means nothing returns early, and description tokens are produced (then truncated to 512).
An empty docs array hits `break` before indexing or saving, total stays 0, and refresh is guarded by `if (total > 0)`. So nothing is saved or refreshed, and the break prevents looping.
